about.title: Personal Injury Help in Colma, California
about.longDescription: Colma is a small city, but its roads carry a steady flow of traffic passing through San Mateo County, and collisions still happen. Public records show 4 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 5 people injured and no traffic deaths reported. Corridors like Hillside Boulevard, Junipero Serra Boulevard, and El Camino Real (SR-82) see the most reported activity, and Friday late mornings into early afternoon show up more often than other times in the data. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in any other kind of accident around town, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering. We offer a free case review for injured people in Colma. Our team can review the details of what happened and explain your options. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover at all.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. We can help sort out how fault gets divided.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Recover for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life. That means your recovery isn't automatically capped just because your medical bills were modest.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed. If there's no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a personal injury claim in Colma?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file most personal injury claims. If a government entity is involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's rarely an automatic bar to a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Colma?
items.answer: Based on public collision records, Hillside Boulevard, Junipero Serra Boulevard, and El Camino Real (SR-82) show the highest counts of reported crashes in Colma, with Friday late morning to early afternoon appearing more frequently than other times. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are personal injury attorneys who review cases directly. We don't represent you until you decide to work with us, and we handle your case ourselves.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we work on contingency. That means we only get paid if there's a recovery in your case.
